haiku-low.q1: Step 4, before the new release starts. The live (old) release must still work on the migrated schema, since migrations are additive.
haiku-low.q2: Only after the release that uses it has been retired. Dropping or renaming waits for a later release.
haiku-low.q3: Each instance passes /healthz three times in a row and smoke tests pass, within 10 minutes. Otherwise aborts: new colour shut down, lock released.
haiku-low.q4: A single step: the public listener is repointed from the live target group to the idle one. No gradual shift.
haiku-low.q5: A 5-minute window above 1% 5xx rate within 15 minutes of the switch. Listener returns to old colour; new colour shut down; migrations stay.
haiku-low.q6: Thirty minutes after the switch, via a rollback job. After that, the old colour is torn down; later problems need a new deploy.
haiku-low.q7: Partly applied, with finished migrations recorded. The deploy stops and releases the lock; the new release never starts; the next run continues the remaining migrations.
haiku-low.q8: The listener decides: the colour it forwards to is live, the other is idle. The state record, its copy, is in parameter store.
haiku-low.q9: A lock in the state record holds the run's CI ID. Held for the whole 30-minute window; released when the run ends unless teardown fails.
haiku-low.q10: A test listener on the same load balancer forwards only to the idle colour, so smoke tests reach the new release while users cannot.
haiku-low.q11: CI runs them in step 4, against the shared PostgreSQL database. Each is recorded when it finishes, so later runs apply only unrecorded ones.
haiku-low.q12: Its instances are shut down. The next deploy finds the idle colour again from the listener.

sonnet.q1: Step 4 (Migrate), after the lock and idle-colour check and before the new release starts on the idle colour. The old release (the one on the live colour) must still work on the migrated schema, since migrations are additive only.
sonnet.q2: Only in a later release, once the release that uses that column or table has been retired.
sonnet.q3: Within 10 minutes of the first instance starting, every instance must pass /healthz three times in a row (checked every 10 s) and the smoke tests must pass via the test listener. If either fails or time runs out, the deploy aborts: the public listener is untouched, the new colour is shut down, the state record is unchanged and the lock is released. Users are not affected.
sonnet.q4: In one step. The public listener is repointed from the live target group to the idle one. There is no gradual shift.
sonnet.q5: Trigger: during the 15-minute watch after the switch, any 5-minute window with a 5xx rate above 1%. Rollback repoints the listener to the old, still-running colour, writes the old colour back as live in the state record, shuts down the new colour's instances, and releases the lock. Migrations are left in place (never reversed). If the repoint fails, it retries and pages an engineer.
sonnet.q6: For 30 minutes after the switch, an engineer can start a rollback job that repoints the listener to the old colour. After the old colour is shut down, a rollback is a normal deploy of the previous release, running all steps including migrations.
sonnet.q7: Partly applied: each finished migration is recorded. The run stops and releases the lock, the new release is never started, the live colour keeps serving, and the listener is unchanged. A failed concurrent index build leaves an invalid index. The next run drops it and runs only the migrations not yet recorded.
sonnet.q8: Step 3 reads which target group the public listener forwards to. That colour is live and the other is idle. The listener is the source of truth, and the state record (a copy, in the cloud parameter store) also holds it. If they disagree, the deploy stops, releases the lock, and a person must check.
sonnet.q9: The deploy lock, a field in the state record that holds the run's CI ID. A second deploy cannot start while it is held. It is held for the whole 30-minute window until teardown (step 11) releases it, or until a run ends/aborts. If teardown fails, it stays held until a person clears it.
sonnet.q10: Through the test listener, a second listener on the same load balancer that forwards only to the idle colour. The document lists it as an open question whether one already exists.
sonnet.q11: CI runs them (step 4), applied once against the shared PostgreSQL database. Each migration is recorded as soon as it finishes, so a later run runs only the unrecorded ones. The document's open questions say it is unconfirmed that the migration tool records each migration. The specific migration tool is NOT STATED.
sonnet.q12: They are shut down in both cases. The old colour stays live and untouched. After an abort the state record is unchanged. After a rollback it is written back to the old colour as live. The lock is released in both. Migrations stay applied, so the next deploy runs only unrecorded migrations. The idle colour then holds no running new release.
